nodes.name: basecommand.rs
nodes.summary: Core types for the execCommand editing API implementing the W3C Editing specification â€” defines the CommandName enum (43 commands), CssPropertyName mapping, value equivalence logic, state/value queries, and command execution dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines a 43-variant CommandName enum, multiple From impls for type conversion, and a comprehensive CssPropertyName enum with style resolution logic for contenteditable. Uses #[expect(unused)] on CommandName to allow forward-looking definitions.

nodes.name: execcommands.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the DocumentExecCommandSupport trait on Document, providing queryCommandSupported/queryCommandState/queryCommandValue/queryCommandEnabled/execCommand entry points that bridge the DOM API to the command execution system per the W3C Editing spec.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a trait extension pattern (DocumentExecCommandSupport) to add execCommand methods to Document. Handles beforeinput/input event dispatch during command execution.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module declaration file registering all 19 execCommand command implementations (backcolor, bold, createlink, delete, fontname, fontsize, forecolor, hilitecolor, insertimage, insertparagraph, italic, removeformat, strikethrough, stylewithcss, subscript, superscript, underline, unlink, and defaultparagraphseparator).

nodes.name: node.rs
nodes.summary: The largest and most comprehensive contenteditable module â€” extends Node with tree manipulation utilities (split_the_parent, wrap_node_list, move_preserving_ranges), command value management (push_down_values, force_the_value, effective_command_value, record/restore), node classification predicates (is_block_node, is_inline_node, is_formattable, is_visible, is_single_line_container, etc.), whitespace canonicalization, and disallowed-ancestor fixing.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive use of inclusive_ancestors traversal, Castable downcasting, and mutable DOM tree manipulation. The NodeOrString enum enables type-flexible child/parent classification.

nodes.name: selection.rs
nodes.summary: Extends Selection with delete_the_selection (a multi-phase deletion algorithm handling block merging, wrapper stripping, and directional deletion) and set_the_selection_value (applies command values to the active range using push_down_values, force_the_value, and clear_the_value). Also defines the EquivalentPoint trait for inline node boundary navigation.

nodes.name: CommandName
nodes.summary: Enum representing all 43 execCommand command names defined by the W3C Editing specification (BackColor, Bold, Copy, CreateLink, Cut, Delete, FontName, FontSize, ForeColor, Italic, Undo, Redo, etc.). Drives command dispatch, state/value queries, and inline formatting behavior.

nodes.name: CssPropertyName
nodes.summary: Enum mapping editing commands to their relevant CSS properties (BackgroundColor, Color, FontFamily, FontSize, FontWeight, FontStyle, TextDecoration, TextDecorationLine). Provides resolved value computation, style attribute parsing, and property set/remove operations on elements.

nodes.name: RecordedStateOfCommand
nodes.summary: Struct recording a command's current state or value override as a BoolOrOptionalString. Provides factory methods for recording per-node, per-document, and override-based state snapshots used for state restoration after preserving-overrides commands.

nodes.name: DefaultSingleLineContainerName
nodes.summary:
Enum representing the default single-line container name for paragraph creation: either Div ('
') or Paragraph ('

'). Controls block-level element creation in editing operations.

nodes.name: BoolOrOptionalString
nodes.summary: Enum representing either a boolean or an optional DOMString value, used for recording command state (bool for inline commands, optional string for value commands) with From impls for type conversion.

nodes.name: DocumentExecCommandSupport
nodes.summary: Trait defining the execCommand API surface for Document: is_command_supported, is_command_indeterminate, command_state_for_command, command_value_for_command, check_support_and_enabled, and exec_command_for_command_id. Bridges DOM queryCommand*/execCommand methods to the command execution system.

nodes.name: EquivalentPoint
nodes.summary: Trait providing inline-node boundary navigation for (Node, offset) pairs â€” previous/next equivalent point traversal, and first/last equivalent point computation. Used by delete_the_selection for fine-grained cursor positioning across inline node boundaries.

nodes.name: SelectionDeleteDirection
nodes.summary: Enum controlling deletion direction (Forward or Backward) for the delete_the_selection algorithm.

nodes.name: SelectionDeletionBlockMerging
nodes.summary: Enum controlling whether adjacent block elements are merged during deletion (Merge or Skip).

nodes.name: SelectionDeletionStripWrappers
nodes.summary: Enum controlling whether wrapper elements are stripped during selection deletion (Strip or NoStrip).

nodes.name: CommandName::execute
nodes.summary: Dispatches a command's action by matching on the CommandName variant and delegating to the corresponding execute_*_command function. Handles override preservation (recording/restoring current states for preserving-overrides commands) around the action.

nodes.name: CommandName::current_state
nodes.summary: Computes the boolean state of a command per the W3C Editing spec â€” handles StyleWithCss (CSS styling flag) specially and uses inline command activated values comparison for inline formatting commands.

nodes.name: CommandName::current_value
nodes.summary: Computes the current value (DOMString) of a command â€” special-cases DefaultParagraphSeparator and FontSize, and delegates to the first formattable contained node's effective command value for standard inline value commands.

nodes.name: CommandName::is_indeterminate
nodes.summary: Determines if a standard inline value command is in an indeterminate state â€” true when effectively contained formatted nodes in the active range have at least two distinct effective command values.

nodes.name: CommandName::is_enabled
nodes.summary: Determines if a command is enabled for a given Range and editing host â€” special-cases the Delete command to check that there is actually content to delete before the cursor.

nodes.name: CommandName::are_equivalent_values
nodes.summary: Implements the equivalent values algorithm from the W3C Editing spec â€” special-cases Bold (700/400 equivalence), color commands (CSS color parsing equivalence), and defaults to string equality.

nodes.name: CssPropertyName::resolved_value_for_node
nodes.summary: Resolves a CSS property's computed value for an element â€” handles BackgroundColor (transparency early-exit and legacy sRGB), Color, FontFamily (detached font element special case), FontSize (manual ancestor traversal for size attributes), FontWeight, FontStyle, and TextDecorationLine.

nodes.name: Document::exec_command_for_command_id
nodes.summary: Implements the execCommand algorithm per the W3C Editing spec â€” checks support/enabled, fires beforeinput event, re-checks enabled state after event, dispatches the matching command's action, and fires input event with the mapped inputType value on success.

nodes.name: Document::check_support_and_enabled
nodes.summary: Checks if a command ID is both supported (mapped to a known CommandName) and enabled (active range exists, editing host valid, command-specific enablement checks pass). Returns the resolved CommandName and Selection on success.

nodes.name: execute_backcolor_command
nodes.summary: Executes the BackColor command â€” validates and normalizes a CSS color value (prepends '#' if missing), rejects invalid colors and currentColor, then sets the selection's background color value.

nodes.name: execute_bold_command
nodes.summary: Executes the Bold command â€” toggles between 'bold' (activate) and 'normal' (deactivate) font-weight values based on the current state queried via queryCommandState.

nodes.name: execute_createlink_command
nodes.summary: Executes the CreateLink command â€” updates href attributes on existing editable anchor elements within the active range, then sets the selection's value to create new links.

nodes.name: maybe_normalize_pixels
nodes.summary: Converts pixel-based font-size command values to legacy font size integers (via legacy_font_size_for), or passes through CSS keyword values unchanged.

nodes.name: font_size_loosely_equivalent
nodes.summary: Checks loose equivalence between font-size values â€” one as a CSS keyword (x-small, small, etc.) and the other as a legacy HTML numeric size (1-7), with bidirectional mapping via css_font_to_font_size.

nodes.name: execute_forecolor_command
nodes.summary: Executes the ForeColor command â€” validates and normalizes a CSS color value (prepends '#' if missing), rejects invalid colors, then sets the selection's foreground color.

nodes.name: serialize_to_simple_color
nodes.summary: Serializes an AbsoluteColor to a simple hex color string (#rrggbb format) by extracting and rounding RGB components.

nodes.name: execute_hilitecolor_command
nodes.summary: Executes the HiliteColor command â€” validates and normalizes a CSS color value (prepends '#' if missing), rejects invalid colors, then sets the selection's highlight (background) color.

nodes.name: Selection::delete_the_selection
nodes.summary: Implements the delete-the-selection algorithm from the W3C Editing spec â€” handles collapsed and non-collapsed ranges, canonicalizes whitespace, navigates equivalent points, handles block merging/wrapper stripping, and performs directional deletion with table and list awareness.

nodes.name: Selection::set_the_selection_value
nodes.summary: Implements the set-the-selection-value algorithm â€” applies a command value to the active range by pushing down values on contained inline nodes, forcing the value on the entire range, or clearing the value for None, with block-extend boundary adjustments.

nodes.name: Node::push_down_values
nodes.summary: Pushes command values down through the DOM tree for a given command, applying inline formatting to text and element nodes by splitting parents, wrapping in new elements, or adjusting existing element attributes and styles.

nodes.name: Node::force_the_value
nodes.summary: Forces a command value on a node range â€” applies the value uniformly by pushing down, then clears the value on the containing block to remove conflicting styling, ensuring the entire selection adopts the new value.

nodes.name: Node::effective_command_value
nodes.summary: Computes the effective command value for a node by traversing inclusive ancestors, collecting specified command values and handling the 'mixed' state for subscript/superscript, then resolving CSS property values for the innermost element with a non-null specified value.

nodes.name: split_the_parent
nodes.summary: Splits the parent of a node list by cloning the parent and moving trailing siblings (after the split point) to the clone, then inserting the clone after the original parent. Used extensively by command operations to restructure the DOM without losing state.

nodes.name: Node::canonicalize_whitespace
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes whitespace at a given offset in a node by collapsing whitespace nodes, collapsing block props, and ensuring consistency for editing operations. Handles both forward and backward canonicalization.

nodes.name: Node::fix_disallowed_ancestors
nodes.summary: Fixes disallowed ancestor elements in the DOM tree by splitting parents and adjusting tag names to ensure the node is a valid child within its editing host per content model rules.

nodes.name: wrap_node_list
nodes.summary: Wraps a list of sibling nodes in a new parent element â€” supports sibling criteria for grouping, and new-parent customization via a closure. Used for creating inline formatting wrappers around text selections.

nodes.name: record_the_values
nodes.summary: Records the current command values and states for a list of nodes, producing a Vec of RecordedValueAndCommandOfNode snapshots used for state restoration after DOM manipulation.

nodes.name: restore_the_values
nodes.summary: Restores previously recorded command values and states to the DOM, reapplying text decorations and sub/superscript wrappers that were captured by record_the_values.

nodes.name: move_preserving_ranges
nodes.summary: Moves a DOM node to a new location while preserving any active Range objects' boundary points by capturing pre-move positions and restoring them post-move, preventing range corruption during tree mutations.

nodes.name: CollapsedBorder
nodes.summary: Represents a border in the CSS collapsing border model with conflict resolution based on style, width, and origin precedence rules.

nodes.name: AbsoluteAxisSolver::solve_margins
nodes.summary: Solves the CSS absolute positioning constraint for a single axis, distributing remaining space to auto margins according to the CSS specification.

nodes.name: ContentSizes::shrink_to_fit
nodes.summary: Computes the shrink-to-fit width (CSS 2.1 section 10.3.5) by clamping the preferred size between min-content and the available width.

nodes.name: TableLayout::layout
nodes.summary: Performs the full CSS table layout: computes column widths, distributes sizes, lays out cells, calculates row heights, resolves collapsed borders, and creates fragments.

nodes.name: TableLayout::compute_table_width
nodes.summary: Computes the final table inline size based on the table's specified width, containing block, and column min/max content sizes using CSS table width algorithms.

nodes.name: TableLayout::do_final_cell_layout
nodes.summary: Performs the final layout pass for each table cell now that column widths and row heights are known, creating fragment trees for cell content.

nodes.name: TableLayout::compute_border_collapse
nodes.summary: Resolves collapsed borders for the entire table grid using CSS border conflict resolution rules (style, width, origin precedence).

nodes.name: TableBuilder::finish
nodes.summary: Finalizes table box tree construction by running missing-cells fixup, column/colgroup geometry adjustment, thead/tfoot reordering, and rowspan finalization.

nodes.name: TaffyContainerContext::compute_child_layout
nodes.summary: Computes intrinsic content sizes for a Taffy grid/flex child by delegating to the child's ComputeInlineContentSizes implementation.

nodes.name: broadcast_change_notification

nodes.name: new

nodes.name: Escape

nodes.name: PaintWorklet

nodes.name: update_rule

nodes.name: AppendRule
nodes.summary: Implements CSSKeyframesRule.appendRule() â€” parses a keyframe selector and block, appends a new keyframe rule, and updates the underlying style data.

nodes.name: DeleteRule
nodes.summary: Implements CSSKeyframesRule.deleteRule() â€” finds and removes a keyframe rule by selector name.

nodes.name: FindRule
nodes.summary: Implements CSSKeyframesRule.findRule() â€” returns a keyframe rule matching the given selector string.

nodes.name: Name
nodes.summary: Returns the animation name (identifier or string) for this @keyframes rule from the underlying style data.

nodes.name: SetName
nodes.summary: Sets the animation name for this @keyframes rule, validating the identifier and updating the underlying style data.

nodes.name: Prefix
nodes.summary: Returns the namespace prefix for this @namespace rule, or null if it is the default namespace.

nodes.name: NamespaceURI
nodes.summary: Returns the namespace URI string for this @namespace rule.

nodes.name: Name
nodes.summary: Returns the custom property name (including leading --) for this @property rule.

nodes.name: Inherits
nodes.summary: Returns whether this custom property inherits by default, as defined by the @property rule's inherits descriptor.

nodes.name: GetInitialValue
nodes.summary: Returns the initial value string for this custom property, or an empty string if none is defined.

nodes.name: cssrulelist.rs
nodes.summary: DOM implementation of the CSSRuleList interface managing an ordered collection of CSS rules with insert, remove, item access, and lazy DOM rule creation.

nodes.name: CSSRuleList
nodes.summary: DOM struct holding a reference to an ordered list of CSS rules with a lazily-populated vector of DOM rule wrappers.

nodes.name: RulesSource
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing between the two rule source types: standard CssRules (from grouping rules) and Keyframes (from @keyframes rules).

nodes.name: new_inherited
nodes.summary: Constructs the inherited portion of a CSSRuleList, computing the rule count based on the RulesSource variant.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Creates a reflected CSSRuleList DOM object wrapping the given rules source.

nodes.name: insert_rule
nodes.summary: Inserts a parsed CSS rule at the given index with type validation, supporting @import restrictions and nesting-relative rule parsing.

nodes.name: remove_rule
nodes.summary: Removes a CSS rule at the given index, deparenting the removed rule and updating the underlying style data.

nodes.name: deparent_all
nodes.summary: Deparents all DOM rule wrappers in this list by calling detach() on each, used when a stylesheet is removed.

nodes.name: item
nodes.summary: Returns the DOM rule at the given index, lazily creating and caching DOM wrappers for style rules as needed.

nodes.name: update_rules
nodes.summary: Synchronizes the rule list with updated style data, updating existing DOM wrappers and creating or removing entries as needed.

nodes.name: cssstyledeclaration.rs
nodes.summary: DOM implementation of the CSSStyleDeclaration interface providing CSS property get/set/remove operations with support for inline styles, computed styles, and rule-based declarations.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a CSSStyleOwner enum to distinguish between element inline styles, rule-based declarations, and computed styles. Contains a large set_property_inner function (85 lines) handling property parsing and validation with shorthand expansion.

nodes.name: CSSStyleDeclaration
nodes.summary: Core DOM struct for CSS property declarations, holding the owner context (element, rule, or computed), readonly flag, and optional pseudo-element selector.

nodes.name: CSSStyleOwner
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing the three style declaration contexts: Element (inline style), CSSRule (rule-based style), and Element (computed style) with a property index.

nodes.name: CSSModificationAccess
nodes.summary: Enum controlling whether a CSSStyleDeclaration is read-write or read-only, based on the declaration source.

nodes.name: mutate_associated_block

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Servo is a prototype web browser engine written in Rust, built as a parallel, modular, and embeddable alternative to traditional monolithic engines. This README introduces the project's goals, supported platforms (macOS, Linux, Windows, OpenHarmony, Android), and provides detailed build instructions. It also links to contribution guidelines, the project wiki, and community channels -- essential context for understanding the tour ahead.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The servoshell binary is the primary desktop application that boots the Servo engine. The main.rs entry point detaches from the Windows console (for GUI mode) and delegates to the servoshell library. The desktop app module orchestrates the full application lifecycle -- initializing the window, setting up the embedding layer, and driving the main event loop that ties input events to browser engine operations.
tour.languageLesson: Rust's `fn main()` is the program entry point. Servo uses a thin binary (main.rs) that delegates to library code, keeping the binary crate minimal and enabling the engine to be embedded in other applications through the `libservo` crate.

tour.title: The Servo Engine Core
tour.description: The servo crate is the central orchestration layer that wires together all major components. The ServoBuilder constructs the engine with configuration, media backends, and platform delegates. The Servo struct owns the constellation (browsing context manager), media thread, and background hang monitor, while the spin_event_loop method drives the engine's main execution loop. This crate exposes the embedder-facing API through WebView handles, making it the bridge between the platform shell and the engine internals.
tour.languageLesson: The Rust Builder pattern (ServoBuilder) provides a fluent API for constructing complex objects with many optional configuration parameters. Each builder method consumes and returns `self`, enabling method chaining before the final `build()` call.

tour.title: Script Engine and the DOM
tour.description: The script component is the largest subsystem, implementing the HTML DOM specification and JavaScript runtime integration. The script_thread.rs file contains the main event loop that processes all DOM-related messages -- managing pipeline spawning, rendering updates, microtask checkpoints, timer scheduling, and WebDriver commands. The DOM module (dom/mod.rs) declares and re-exports over 70 DOM submodules covering all web platform APIs from HTML elements to WebGPU, WebXR, and Web Audio. This is where the browser's document model comes to life, backed by SpiderMonkey for JavaScript execution.
tour.languageLesson: Servo's script thread maps closely to the HTML specification's 'event loop' concept. Each browsing context runs tasks from multiple task sources (DOM manipulation, networking, timers, etc.) with spec-mandated prioritization. The microtask queue (for Promise callbacks) is drained before each new macrotask -- a critical ordering guarantee for web compatibility.

tour.title: Core DOM Primitives: Document, Node, and Events
tour.description: Three foundational types underpin the entire DOM implementation. The Node struct (node.rs) provides over 200 methods for tree manipulation, traversal, and cloning -- every DOM element, text node, and comment inherits from this. The Document (document.rs) implements the full DOM Document interface including loading, parsing, rendering coordination, and event dispatch. The Event system (event.rs) defines the core event dispatching algorithm with propagation path management (capture, target, bubble phases) that all DOM events rely on. Understanding these three types is essential for grasping how the rest of the DOM layer is structured.
tour.languageLesson: The DOM uses a prototype-chain inheritance model. In Servo's Rust implementation, this is modeled through composition and trait-based dispatch. Each DOM interface (e.g., HTMLElement) wraps a Node internally and uses Rust's trait system to expose spec-compliant inheritance -- a fundamentally different approach from C++ browser engines that use actual class hierarchies.

tour.title: Layout Engine
tour.description: The layout component computes the visual geometry of web content. The LayoutThread (layout_impl.rs) manages the full layout pipeline: stylesheet handling, reflow triggering, stacking context tree construction, and display list generation. The FragmentTree (fragment_tree.rs) holds the root fragment hierarchy -- the output of layout computation that maps DOM elements to positioned, sized boxes. The construct_modern.rs module implements the modern box-tree construction logic with flexbox and grid awareness, creating the intermediate box tree structures that handle anonymous block wrappers and table anonymous objects before the final fragment tree is built.
tour.languageLesson: Servo's layout engine uses a two-phase approach: first, a 'box tree' is constructed from the DOM and style data (handling anonymous boxes for inline/block nesting); second, the box tree is converted into a 'fragment tree' that assigns final positions and sizes. This separation enables incremental layout -- only the subtrees affected by a DOM mutation need recomputation.

tour.title: Pipeline Management and the Constellation
tour.description: The constellation is Servo's multi-process browsing context coordinator. The Constellation struct (constellation.rs) manages all browsing contexts, pipelines, event loops, IPC message routing, navigation, session history, and process sandboxing decisions. Each Pipeline (pipeline.rs) represents a document processing pipeline -- tracking its browsing context, event loop, child frames, history state, and load data. This architecture enables Servo to isolate web content in separate OS processes, with the constellation acting as the central authority that routes messages between pipelines and the compositor.
tour.languageLesson: The constellation implements the 'actor model' pattern -- each pipeline, compositor, and the constellation itself communicate exclusively through message passing via typed IPC channels. This design eliminates shared mutable state between processes, a key requirement for both security (site isolation) and Rust's ownership model.

tour.title: Networking and Resource Loading
tour.description: The networking component handles all HTTP requests, WebSocket connections, and resource fetching. The resource_thread.rs initializes the async runtime and creates separate public/private resource channels for cookie isolation. The http_loader.rs implements the core Fetch specification -- constructing requests, handling CORS preflight, managing redirects, processing authentication, and setting cookies. Together these files form the pipeline that fetches every HTML document, CSS stylesheet, JavaScript file, image, and media resource that the browser renders.
tour.languageLesson: Servo uses Tokio's async runtime for network I/O, with a dedicated resource thread that bridges async Rust futures to the synchronous message-passing world of the constellation and script thread. This hybrid approach keeps the networking layer non-blocking while maintaining the deterministic message ordering required by the HTML spec.

tour.title: Painting and Compositing
tour.description: The paint component bridges layout output to the screen. The Paint subsystem (paint.rs) orchestrates WebRender instances, processes display lists from layout, drives CSS animations, and handles touch/scroll input. The Painter (painter.rs) manages per-context WebRender documents, constructs display lists from fragment trees, and applies scroll/zoom updates. Servo uses Mozilla's WebRender GPU-based rendering engine, which enqueues drawing commands into a scene graph and rasterizes them on the GPU for smooth 60fps rendering.
tour.languageLesson: WebRender separates rendering into two phases: scene building (CPU-side construction of a display list from layout fragments) and frame building (GPU-side rasterization of the scene into pixels). This architecture offloads compositing, blending, and transform animation to the GPU, enabling smooth scrolling and CSS transforms without repainting.

tour.title: SVG Rendering Engine
tour.description: The SVG engine is a dedicated subsystem for rendering SVG content independently of the HTML/CSS layout pipeline. The render_tree.rs builds an intermediate render tree from parsed SVG DOM nodes, capturing shapes, text, gradients, patterns, and transforms. The traversal.rs module walks this render tree depth-first, applying coordinate transforms and dispatching each node to specialized shape renderers. The shapes module defines a Shape enum spanning all SVG primitive types (Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Line, Path, Polygon, Polyline), each with its own clip geometry computation. The renderer module provides the concrete WebRender drawing code for each shape and style component. A comprehensive manual test suite in test_svg_engine.html validates rendering across ~60 test cases spanning 14 feature categories including gradients, patterns, transforms, clipping, masking, and filter effects.
tour.languageLesson: SVG rendering differs fundamentally from HTML/CSS layout. Instead of the box-model flow layout, SVG uses a painter's model -- elements are drawn in document order, later elements paint on top of earlier ones, and coordinate systems cascade through nested `<g>` groups and `<use>` instantiations via transformation matrices. The `viewBox` attribute establishes a local coordinate system that maps to the viewport, enabling resolution-independent scaling.

tour.title: SVG Integration with DOM and Layout
tour.description: The SVG engine does not exist in isolation -- it integrates into Servo through the DOM script bindings and the layout system. The DOM SVG module (svggraphicselement.rs, svgsvgelement.rs) provides the JavaScript-accessible interface for SVG elements, connecting them to the rest of the DOM tree and enabling script-based SVG manipulation. The layout SVG module (svg/builder.rs, svg/mod.rs) bridges the SVG engine into the layout pipeline, constructing SVG-specific fragment types and handling viewport/coordinate system setup. This two-way integration means SVG content participates fully in the DOM tree (supporting events, queries, and mutations) while also flowing through the layout pipeline for proper sizing and positioning.

tour.title: Build System, CI/CD and Development Infrastructure
tour.description: The workspace-level Cargo.toml defines the Servo monorepo -- declaring workspace members (servoshell, capi, xpath, svg_engine, media), shared package metadata, and centralized dependency versions. The servo crate's Cargo.toml shows how rendering backends are selected through feature flags. The main CI pipeline (main.yml) dynamically generates a test matrix using Python, running builds and tests across Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and OpenHarmony on every push to main and every pull request. The devcontainer Dockerfile builds a complete Servo development environment with Ubuntu 24.04, Rust 1.95.0, and all required system dependencies -- enabling contributors to start hacking with a single command.
tour.languageLesson: Cargo workspaces allow multiple related Rust crates to share a single `Cargo.lock` file and `target/` build directory, ensuring consistent dependency versions across the entire project. The `[workspace.dependencies]` section in the root Cargo.toml centralizes version declarations -- individual crate manifests reference these with `workspace = true`, making dependency updates a single-line change.
